Assuming that all side faces have the same height of $9\,\text{m}$, find the total surface area of the square pyramid above using its net.
worked_solution:
The net of our pyramid is the following.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930500/assets/09eff98ca31b4bb350e2d793dcfa6e6972de25bb3b613c898533068c36fe9a78.png)

$$

$$

First, notice that the base of the pyramid is a square with a side equal to $2\,\text{m}.$ Hence:

$$
\text{Area of the square}=2\times 2=4\,{\text{m}}^{2}.
$$

 

Each side face of our solid is triangle, where the base is $2\,\text{m}$ and the height is $9\,\text{m}.$ Therefore:

$$
\text{Area of the triangle}=\frac{1}{2}\times 2\times 9=9\,{\text{m}}^{2}.
$$

Finally, the surface area of the pyramid consists of $1$ square (base) and $4$ triangles (side faces). 

Therefore, we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Surface area} & =(\text{Area of the square})+4\times (\text{Area of the triangle}) \\  & =4+4\times 9 \\  & =4+36 \\  & =40\,{\text{m}}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
